ADOMs and products

SATOM's six workspaces (Global, FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer, FortiGate) — what each is for, how to switch between them, and how data is kept separate.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsappliances.view_maintenance
📍 WhereTop bar → Switch Product (URL /product/select) · sidebar → ‹ Global · Global sidebar → ADOMs · Settings → Fleet & Devices → ADOMs

What an ADOM is#

An ADOM (administrative domain) is a workspace inside SATOM scoped to one product family, in the style of FortiManager ADOMs. Every ADOM shares the same look, but has its own sidebar menu, its own appliances, and its own jobs, notifications, bookmarks, templates and scheduled actions.

ℹ️Note

In SATOM, ADOM means a SATOM workspace. A FortiWeb appliance can also have its own administrative domains; SATOM registers such an appliance once per appliance-side ADOM. The sidebar then shows ADOM: under the selected device. Do not confuse the two.

The six ADOMs#

ADOM Home Purpose
Global / One console over the whole fleet: dashboard, monitoring, search, Architecture and Service Diagram, fleet objects, jobs, certificates, and SATOM administration. See Global home.
FortiWeb /web/ Web application firewall management: FortiWeb's own menu for the selected device (server policies, server objects, web protection, system settings …), the device-scoped WAF tools under Operations → WAF, backups, firmware.
FortiADC /adc/ Application delivery: the appliance's own menu (load balancing, WAF, network security …), signatures and an API console. See FortiADC.
FortiAuthenticator /fac/ Identity and access: local, LDAP and RADIUS identities, user groups, FortiTokens, issued certificates and the RADIUS/TACACS+ clients. See FortiAuthenticator.
FortiAnalyzer /faz/ Logging and analytics through the JSON-RPC API: the unit's own menu when a layout exists for its build, otherwise SATOM's curated FortiAnalyzer menu. See FortiAnalyzer.
FortiGate /fgt/ Next-generation firewall, read live over the REST API: the device's measured GUI pages edit cmdb objects (dry run first, verified), the API console writes to /api/v2/cmdb/ only (dry-run by default), the section pages are read-only. See FortiGate.

The list is data, not code. The ADOMs are rows in a database table that an administrator edits in Settings → Fleet & Devices → ADOMs: name, tagline, description, logo, order, whether the ADOM is active, and which shared capabilities it offers (personal banner, API tokens, firmware, naming rules, regex lab). An inactive ADOM disappears from the chooser. Global, FortiWeb and FortiADC are core and cannot be deleted — only deactivated; another ADOM cannot be deleted while appliances are still registered in it.

What a device ADOM's sidebar holds#

Each device ADOM draws the device's own menu, built from the GUI layouts measured on the selected device's firmware build, inside the same SATOM groups in every ADOM: ‹ Global, Device, Operations (the fleet pages first, then the backup entries), the device menu, Automation (with the API console as a sub-menu), Administrator and Plugins. An entry whose page does not work for that product is greyed out and says why on hover. The Global ADOM has no device menu; it draws the Global block, ADOMs, Automation and Administrator. See Navigation for every group and entry.

Switching ADOM#

From How
Any page Top bar → Switch Product (product logo with arrows) → pick a card → Open →
A product ADOM Sidebar → ‹ Global (always the first entry)
The Global ADOM Sidebar → ADOMs → the product
The Global home Click a product's card ( ADOM · appliance(s) · open ›)

After you sign in, a session without a chosen ADOM starts in Global.

The ADOM is per browser tab#

Each browser tab remembers its own ADOM. You can work in FortiWeb in one tab and FortiADC in another; switching in one tab does not change the other. A new tab, or a page opened by typing its address, starts in the ADOM you switched to most recently.

The selected device is per ADOM#

Per-device pages use an implicit selected device rather than asking each time. Each ADOM keeps its own selection, so choosing a FortiAuthenticator does not change the FortiWeb you were working on. Use the device area of the top bar (Switch device) to change it. If you can see exactly one appliance in an ADOM, it is used without asking.

How data is kept apart#

You are in… You see
Global Everything, from every product.
FortiWeb FortiWeb rows, plus older rows that were never stamped with a product (they predate multi-product support).
FortiADC / FortiAuthenticator / FortiAnalyzer / FortiGate Only that product's rows.

This applies to appliances, jobs, notifications, bookmarks, templates and scheduled actions. Opening another ADOM's appliance by its ID answers not found. A record you create inside a product ADOM is stamped with that product; a record created from Global is unscoped.

Appliances in maintenance mode are additionally hidden from users without appliances.view_maintenance.

💡Tip

An appliance whose product matches no active ADOM is still listed on the Global home, with its product key shown as a grey badge — Global is the only console that can still show it.

Troubleshooting#

"This ADOM can only add appliances."#

Possible causes — you tried to register an appliance of another product while inside a product ADOM.

Solution — switch to that product's ADOM (or Global) and add it there.

A page shows a different product than the tab I am looking at#

Solution — check the ADOM: badge in the top bar. Reload the tab; if needed, switch explicitly with Switch Product.

An ADOM is missing from the chooser#

Possible causes — it was deactivated in Settings → ADOMs.

Solution — an administrator re-activates it.

Advanced How the active ADOM is resolved

For every request SATOM decides the ADOM in this order: the URL scope (/web/, /adc/ …), then the X-ADOM header each tab sends, then a hidden _adom form field, then the session default. Only explicit switches (the chooser, the ADOM links, / and /web/) change the session default; ordinary navigation never does. Link prefetching on hover is disabled so hovering an ADOM link can never switch it. The registry is cached for 15 seconds, so an edit in Settings → ADOMs reaches every worker within that time.
